label: Adenoid_Cystic_Carcinoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts

- Most cases arise in minor salivary glands of the head and neck, especially the palate
- Biphasic tumor with both ductal (luminal) and myoepithelial (abluminal) cells
- Classic microscopic cribriform ("Swiss cheese") pattern with basophilic basement-membrane–like material
- Marked tendency for perineural invasion and infiltrative growth
- Prognosis: high rate of local recurrence and delayed distant metastasis (notably to lung); 5-year survival relatively good, but 15- to 20-year survival poor

## Terminology

- Definition: Malignant biphasic epithelial neoplasm of salivary gland origin demonstrating cribriform, tubular, and/or solid growth, with dual cell population, often showing perineural invasion
- Synonyms: Cylindroma (outdated; not recommended)
- Abbreviation: AdCC

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria

- **Essential:**
  - Biphasic tumor composed of admixed ductal (luminal) and myoepithelial (abluminal, often basaloid) cells [Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html)
  - At least one of three architectural patterns: cribriform, tubular, or solid (cribriform most characteristic)
  - Basophilic, hyaline, basement-membrane–like material within lumina of tumor nests
  - Demonstration of perineural invasion
- **Desirable:**
  - Detection of MYB::NFIB gene fusion, or less commonly MYBL1::NFIB, in tumor cells
  - Positive immunohistochemical staining for MYB
  - Necrosis, high mitotic activity, or overgrowth of solid component suggesting high grade transformation in aggressive cases

## Etiology/Pathogenesis

- Nearly all cases harbor MYB::NFIB gene fusion (translocation), with rare MYBL1::NFIB fusion [Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html)
- Resulting overexpression of MYB oncogene implicated in tumorigenesis

## Clinical Issues

  - **Epidemiology:**
    - Represents ~23% of all salivary gland carcinomas ([Textbooks, page 304](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=304))
    - No gender predilection
    - Most patients present in 5th–7th decades
  - **Site:**
    - ~50–70% of AdCC arises in minor salivary glands of head and neck; palate most common site
    - Among major glands, parotid is most frequently affected ([Textbooks, page 304](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=304); [Textbooks, page 1062](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Atlas.pdf#page=1062))
    - May occur anywhere in upper aerodigestive tract, including parotid, submandibular, hard/soft palate, and lip
  - **Presentation:**
    - Typically presents as firm, slow-growing, painless mass, but can ulcerate or invade nerves causing pain/paresthesia
  - **Natural History:**
    - Infiltrative with strong proclivity for perineural invasion ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
    - Recurrences and distant metastases (especially to lung) may develop after prolonged intervals
  - **Prognosis:**
    - 5-year survival ~70%
    - 15-year survival ~10% ([Textbooks, page 304](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=304))
    - Prognosis worsens with solid growth pattern, perineural invasion, or high-grade transformation

## Macroscopic

- Firm, infiltrative masses, sometimes with areas of necrosis ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
- May be relatively circumscribed but often show finger-like infiltration at periphery
- Cut surfaces may appear gray-white, solid, with foci of cystic change and sometimes hyaline areas
- ![Cut section of ACC, turbinate to palate](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticgross01.jpg)
- ![Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the palate](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_oral/hn_oral_p0305_fig01_figure_8_49.jpeg)

## Microscopic

- Patterns: cribriform (most characteristic), tubular, and solid ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
  - Cribriform: nests of small basaloid cells with multiple cylindrical pseudocystic spaces filled with basophilic (PAS+, type IV collagen) basement-membrane–like material ("Swiss cheese" appearance)
    - ![Cribriform pattern](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu03new.jpg)
    - ![AdCC, cribriform pattern, textbook figure](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_oral/hn_oral_p0305_fig05_figure_8_50.jpeg)
  - Tubular: ducts lined by cuboidal epithelial cells, surrounded by myoepithelial (abluminal) cells
    - ![Tubular pattern](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu02new.jpg)
  - Solid: solid nests of basaloid cells, high nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio, often associated with higher grade, increased mitoses, and necrosis
    - ![Solid pattern](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu04new.jpg)
- Biphasic cell population:
  - Ductal/luminal cells: central, cuboidal, sometimes eosinophilic, lining true ducts
  - Myoepithelial/abluminal ("basaloid") cells: peripheral in nests, with scant cytoplasm
  - ![Dual cell population and tubular/cribriform areas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_thompson/hn_thompson_p0337_fig01_figure_13_26.jpg)
- Perineural invasion is common and may be extensive ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
  - ![Perineural invasion](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu06new.jpg)
- Basement-membrane–like matrix is PAS positive
- Features that suggest aggressive or high-grade transformation:
  - Increased mitotic figures
  - Necrosis (comedo-like or otherwise)
  - Loss of biphasic cell organization
  - ![High grade transformation](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu05new.jpg)
- Other variants: clear cell change, squamous metaplasia ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
  - ![Clear myoepithelial cells](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu09new.jpg)
  - ![Squamous metaplasia](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu08new.jpg)

## Ancillary Tests

- Immunohistochemistry:
  - MYB: nuclear positivity in most cases ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html)); useful for confirmation
  - Cytokeratins (CAM5.2): highlights ductal/luminal cells
    - ![CAM5.2](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu12new.jpg)
  - Myoepithelial markers:
    - p40, p63: peripheral/abluminal myoepithelial cell staining
      - ![p40](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu10new.jpg)
    - SMA, calponin: abluminal myoepithelial cells
      - ![SMA](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu11new.jpg)
- Molecular:
  - MYB::NFIB gene fusion (majority), less often MYBL1::NFIB ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
- Cytology:
  - Scant, small, uniform basaloid cells, forming clusters with hyaline globules; dual cell population may be seen ([Pathology Outlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu14new.jpg))

## Differential Diagnosis

- **Polymorphous low-grade adenocarcinoma (PLGA):**
  - More cytologic uniformity, lower degree of cytologic atypia, lacks prominent basement-membrane–like material
  - Less tendency for perineural invasion than AdCC
  - Immunophenotype differs: PLGA shows p631/p402, AdCC p631/p401 ([Textbooks, page 304](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=304))
  - Lack of MYB fusion in PLGA
- **Basal cell adenocarcinoma:**
  - Basaloid cells but absence of cribriform pattern and not typically biphasic
  - No abundant basophilic matrix material
  - Lacks strong perineural invasion seen in AdCC
  - Different immunoprofile (less prominent myoepithelial markers)
- **Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma:**
  - May show transitions from benign pleomorphic adenoma to carcinoma
  - More pleomorphic cytology, may display areas resembling various carcinomas, including AdCC, but history and presence of residual PA areas help ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Carcinoma_Ex_Pleomorphic_Adenoma.html))
  - May lack uniform cribriform/tubular patterns
- **Mucoepidermoid carcinoma:**
  - Mucinous and intermediate cell types, lacks biphasic ductal/myoepithelial architecture
  - No cribriform/cylindromatous pattern or abundant basement-membrane–like material
- **Epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma:**
  - Also biphasic but has hyalinized stroma with clear cell myoepithelial layer; lacks classic cribriform or solid pattern
  - Usually negative for MYB rearrangement ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Epithelial_Myoepithelial_Carcinoma.html))
- **HPV-related multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma:**
  - Basaloid and surface-derived features, but positive for transcriptionally active high-risk HPV; distinguished by HPV-specific assays ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Hpv_Related_Multiphenotypic_Sinonasal_Carcinoma.html))

cards.excerpt: Entity: HPV-related multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma definition: HPV-related multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma (HMSC) is an epithelial neoplasm exhibiting features of both surface-derived and minor salivary gland–derived elements, harbouring transcriptionally active HPV. related_terminology: Acceptable: HPV-associated multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma. Not recommended: HPV-related carcinoma with adenoid cystic–like features. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: a carcinoma composed of basaloid type cells; high-risk HPV by HPV-specific assay (not p16 alone); myoepithelial differentiation by immunohistochemistry. Desirable: sinonasal tract location; ductal differentiation; overlying squamous dysplasia.

cards.title: Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma Section: cytology FNAB smears can show poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma or salivary duct carcinoma, or other salivary gland carcinomas including mucoepidermoid carcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, and carcinosarcoma, or the FNAB may show PA, depending on sampling. It is uncommon that both components are identified, and necrosis in an otherwise pleomorphic adenoma may be the only clue apart from a previous history of a longstanding mass or previous biopsy.

cards.excerpt: Entity: Sialoblastoma Section: differential_diagnosis The primitive histological features and the patients young age help to differentiate sialoblastoma from other basaloid salivary gland tumours such as basal cell adenoma/adenocarcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, and adamantinoma-like Ewing sarcoma.

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Clinical features
cards.excerpt:

5 year overall survival 55 - 89%
15 year or 20 year survival is dismal, in the range of 20 - 40%

Lung is most common site of distant metastasis (Head Neck 2017;39:456)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Lung metastases
cards.excerpt:
Prognostic factors
Independent prognostic predictors include AJCC TNM staging, margin status, high mitotic index (defined as ≥ 5 per 10 high power fields) and solid architecture (Am J Surg Pathol 2017;41:1422)
Presence and percentage of solid architecture reflects clinical outcome and should be reported in the pathology report
Some studies showed that the presence but not the percentage of solid growth is an independent predictor for adverse outcome (Am J Surg Pathol 2017;41:1422, Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Ora Radio 2013;115:368, Head Neck 2017;39:456)
Other studies show that tumors with higher percentage of solid pattern, defined as 30% or more, are associated with increased risk of recurrence and decreased survival (Cancer 1984;54:1062, Cancer 1978;42:265)

Most patients receive adjuvant radiation therapy given the high rate of local recurrence and dismal long term survival
